requirements.requirement: Establish a persistent integrity baseline covering /etc on node1.
requirements.summary: AIDE was installed and configured with a recursive /etc rule. A protected 1,109-entry database was promoted, and direct plus service-driven checks against the final baseline reported no differences.

requirements.requirement: Enable later changes within /etc to be identified and reported.
requirements.summary: A bounded test file added under /etc was explicitly reported as an added entry with AIDE exit status 5. The marker was subsequently removed. The final configuration continues to check file type, permissions, ownership, size, links, ACLs, SELinux labels, extended attributes, and SHA-256/SHA-512 hashes, with reports sent to a log and stdout.

overall_summary: The task outcomes are satisfied. Node1 has a clean, persistent AIDE baseline for all of /etc, and captured behavior demonstrates that a later addition is identified and reported. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, and recovered system, timer, database, and clean integrity check are directly shown and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot observations.
limitations: The synthetic change-detection test preceded the final removal of volatile inode/time/link-count attributes and final database promotion. The final rule still retains content hashes and security attributes that detect substantive file changes, but no second synthetic change was introduced against that exact final database.
Lifecycle snapshots are bounded and do not independently inventory the AIDE configuration or database; those final states are established by executor command evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation, configuration and database promotion, recurring-check units, corrective removal of reboot-sensitive metadata attributes, and reboot were causally connected to the outcome or mandatory evidence protocol. The temporary detection marker was bounded and removed. Final observations show no failed services, no new listening exposure, healthy package management, and only normal reboot-associated temporary-file and process-ID changes.
